---
title: "3 Decisions, price and watch"
---

A score decides nothing. Session 3 builds the four decisions that consume it: adjudication
turns a PD into Approve, Refer or Decline; pricing turns a booked loan into a return on equity
against a hurdle; early warning ranks the book for deterioration and names the triggers; line
increase offers more credit only where risk and economics clear together. Each is gated or
checked in its own way, and each can matter as much as the model under it. The session ends
with the loan workbench, the same four decisions for one loan at a time, rebuilt by prompting
an agent on the same engine.

## The videos

Seven chapters, one idea each, in session order.

{{< yt S3-c1 >}}

One score, four decisions: what each decision consumes from the score spine, and why a
decision layer can matter as much as the model.

{{< yt S3-c2 >}}

Adjudication: hard knockouts decline whatever the PD, PD zones sort the rest, and refer
overrides send thin files to a person. Over all applicants, as the portal decides them —
a description of what it decides, not a performance measure: the model was trained on
four in five of these rows, so their PDs are in-sample — Approve {{< var adj.book.Approve.n >}}, Refer {{< var adj.book.Refer.n >}}, Decline
{{< var adj.book.Decline.n >}}. Most Declines are knockouts, not the model
([D5.3](../mdd/adjudication/methodology.qmd#adj-knockouts-dominate)).

{{< yt S3-c3 >}}

Pricing is one fraction: the return on equity a loan earns at its quoted rate, against a
hurdle of {{< var market.roe_hurdle >}}. Simple arithmetic with subjective inputs, and
deterministic — the platform lists pricing as a tool, not a model.

{{< yt S3-c4 >}}

Of the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked loans, {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} clear the hurdle at
their quoted rates; the video calls the rest's exposure, \${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}},
"below the hurdle". It teaches how the profit waterfall and the hurdle test work, and that a
quote can only be judged against the bank's own PD. It does not show a pricing practice: the
generator quotes without the capital charge, so the level is a property of the data
([D6.7, finding 1](../mdd/pricing/limitations.qmd)). And "worst" needs a measure: by share of
loans, mispricing is worst in band {{< var pricing.worst_band >}}
({{< var pricing.worst_band_rate >}}); by mispriced exposure, in band
{{< var pricing.worst_ead_band >}}
([D6.5](../mdd/pricing/performance.qmd#pr-by-band)). Homework H3.2 is about exactly that.

{{< yt S3-c5 >}}

Early warning predicts a different target, and its gate is on the action — call the riskiest
tenth and capture at least {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} of future deterioration — with the
AUC, {{< var ews.auc >}}, reported, not gated. On held-out accounts the model captures
{{< var ews.capture >}}. Over the whole book it appears to capture
{{< var ews.whole.capture >}}, because most of the book is its own training data
([D7.5](../mdd/ews/performance.qmd#ews-held-out-vs-whole-book)). Always quote the held-out
figure.

{{< yt S3-c6 >}}

Line increase: four clauses and the smallest of three caps, walked through on two accounts,
then the funnel over the book — {{< var li.funnel.book.n >}} booked accounts,
{{< var li.funnel.pd.n >}} after the probability and PD clauses,
{{< var li.funnel.amount.n >}} with a positive amount, {{< var li.funnel.roe.n >}} offers. The
video's lesson is that a funnel which says no to most of the book is protecting it. D8 adds
that all {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_cannot_fail >}} of the gates that check the offered cohort
cannot fail — {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_by_construction >}} by construction,
{{< var li.cohort_gate.n_on_this_book >}} on this book — so the restraint is the rules', and the
gate does not test it
([D8.3](../mdd/line_increase/methodology.qmd),
[D8.7, finding 1](../mdd/line_increase/limitations.qmd)).

{{< yt S3-c7 >}}

The loan workbench (v2): rebuilt by prompting an agent, beside the untouched portfolio portal
(v1), with no new analytics. Every number on its screen comes from the module that owns it,
and every what-if must equal the batch result exactly. Then: prompt your own agent to
improve one module.

## Read

The four module chapters of the Model Documentation tab, each in the same nine parts as D4:

- [D5, Loan Adjudication](../mdd/adjudication/index.qmd) — the model, the policy layer and
  the decision mix.
- [D6, Pricing](../mdd/pricing/index.qmd) — the engine's arithmetic, what the tool reports
  about the book, and why the level of mispricing describes the data.
- [D7, Early Warning](../mdd/ews/index.qmd) — a gate on capture, an AUC reported against the
  data's own ceiling, tiers and named triggers.
- [D8, Line Increase](../mdd/line_increase/index.qmd) — the funnel, the amount rules and the
  incremental economics.

How the four depend on the score is [D3](../mdd/d3-dependencies.qmd); how the workbench is
held to the batch pipeline is in [D9](../mdd/d9-implementation.qmd) and in each chapter's
"who consumes it" section.

## Notebook, lab and workbench

- Notebook: [`notebooks/03_04_adjudication_pricing_monitoring.ipynb`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/notebooks/03_04_adjudication_pricing_monitoring.ipynb)
  — one section per decision, then one account followed through all four. Its flowcharts
  are mermaid diagrams; the Codespace installs the VS Code extension that draws them.
- Lab: [`workshop/labs/S3_4-lab.md`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/workshop/labs/S3_4-lab.md)
  — adjudication, pricing, monitoring and line increases, by hand or with an agent, ending in
  a decision memo for one account.
- Workbench: run `make run`, then open the portfolio portal at `http://localhost:8100` and
  the loan workbench at `http://localhost:8100/v2`. In a Codespace, open the forwarded port
  8100 from the *Ports* tab. Pick a loan, read its four tabs, and move a slider: the what-if
  re-runs the same module function the batch run uses. Nothing is saved.

Session 3 runs on `main`. If you prefer to work from a stage tag, it must be `stage-4` or
later, never `stage-3` — `main`'s portal cannot load at `stage-3`:

```bash
git stash -u
git checkout stage-4
git checkout main -- app notebooks workshop wiki
python verify.py
```

The homework assumes `main` (`git checkout main`).

## Check

```bash
make stop
python verify.py
```

`make stop` shuts down the portal if it is still running. The adjudication, early warning
and line increase lines check each model's gates against its saved model. The apps line
starts the portal in-process, calls an endpoint of every module, compares the priced book
with the committed pricing summary, and checks that a workbench what-if sent with no
changes returns the batch decision.

## Homework with an agent

Three exercises: move a policy threshold through `decide` and explain why the decision mix
moves the way it does; catch an agent that says mispricing is worst in band D; and audit a
what-if that re-tiers the watchlist from a rounded column — a defect the workbench's first
build had, which the final review caught before it was merged. Each has a self-check: [Session 3 homework](homework-s3.qmd).
